second_order: figuring out r/place and finding the work
theme_note: People ask what the event, image, location, or procedure is and answer with links, coordinates, explanations, or checks.

second_order: using the Irish-language thread to make sense of April Fools
theme_note: People use an existing weekly Irish-language format to correct its title, explain r/place, and joke about other April Fools material; the format predates the canvas.

second_order: making, growing, and mending the fleg
theme_note: People place, size, extend, outline, repair, maintain, and report the Irish flag as a shared object; what they put inside it varies.

second_order: working out what goes on the fleg
theme_note: People propose, revise, praise, reject, or joke through slogans, figures, colours, and decorations for the Irish patch.

second_order: holding the line against the Void and other attacks
theme_note: People warn of damage, recruit defenders, repair attacks, and celebrate holding ground; the named threat and confidence vary.

second_order: calling raids and taking more canvas
theme_note: People propose or pursue overwriting other flags, spreading beyond the patch, or taking opportunistic space; replies sometimes refuse or redirect the call.

second_order: mocking, disputing, and tiring of pixel work
theme_note: People challenge the value, seriousness, truth, or legitimacy of participation and answer those challenges; this includes disagreement not reducible to a design choice.
People negotiate borders, protect or adopt adjacent art, ask and answer help, and describe alliances or compromise; welcome, refusal, and disputed ownership all occur.

second_order: staging the room's own April Fools joke
theme_note: A non-canvas post springs a false Vatican claim and the replies recognise, thank, and extend the joke.

second_order: herding plans into megathreads, scripts, and Discord
theme_note: People concentrate discussion, hand plans between threads and venues, automate maintenance, correct competing scripts, and police surplus posts.

second_order: checking whether an edit really saved
theme_note: People test a British-flag edit across tabs and an incognito window, name a timeout glitch, and report its disappearance.

second_order: recruiting the room for side causes
theme_note: Short posts ask people to join memorial or other named canvas causes without enough surviving response to fold them into the flag work.

second_order: turning a proposed drawing into a personal row
theme_note: A help request becomes an extended exchange about greatness, freedom, sincerity, and the people arguing rather than practical pixel work.

second_order: cleaning up and carrying the picture home
theme_note: People fetch, photograph, correct, frame, revise, or reuse the finished canvas and its imagery in banners and keepsakes.

second_order: marking the stop and thanking the pixel workers
theme_note: Once placement stops, people mourn, celebrate, thank contributors, allocate credit, and explain what the collaboration meant.

second_order: keeping canvas friendships going after place
theme_note: Former neighbours exchange thanks, hospitality, gifts, music, invitations, jokes, and game talk after the shared canvas work.
